commit.message: Bump up version number in man page
Bump up version number in man page
Add the class handling barcode summary metadata
Implement dup and lowmapq count summary output
Implement the count for total and unmapped.
Fix an issue of not outputing the summary statistics.
Update readme. Use true num_dup as much as possible.
Update manual

Use a func to add indexing options.

Also format the code.
Use separate functions to add options.
Support wildcards in read file names.
Update the README on using wildcards in file names.
Update version.
Move li_dev4's content to li_dev5, including no-sorting read-format, and overflow of fragment length
Add more include for stdint
Add more include for stdint
Output duplication number in bulk bed format too.
Fix a bug in summary the alignment stats when outputing SAM format
Update readme
Bump up version number
Add some debug information when reading the temporary file
Update manpage link in README.md
Use local directory to hold tempoary files when the output file is to stdout or stderr
Bump up version number
max_num_mappings_in_mem when using too many temp files
Add a warning message about temp file size. Decrease the temp file doubling threshold to 850.
Do not count the barcode that is not in the whitelist in the summary
Add the row that summarize the number of fragments that can not be barcode corrected
Fix an issue of MD string, where 0 is inserted between adjacent mismatches and the end of the MD string
added debug code and options/added cache size, cache param, all reads options/parallelized cache update
added option for frip est. params/compute est. frip for every barcode/include in summary file
added options/code for num cache slots computation/turned it on by default/outputs in summary file
fixed bug with cardinality estimation when sketch is not completely full
add check in output to make avoid NaNs in summary file
added debug code to print out caceh stats at end of execution
updated README with summary file information
fix small typo in README
removed the --use-all-reads option
hide some cache-related options in the developmental options section
updated parameters for logit function; add inverse logit when printing summary
update parameters to correct ones for logit model
removed reduction for cache_hits_per_batch variable to avoid compilation issue
bump version number
Update readme to clarify some details about the QC metrics
Fix a serious issue of comparing SAM mapping record that causes paired-end dedup errors
Fix an issue of keeping wrong mapq read during deduplication
Bump up version
Significantly improve the scalability by parsing input fastq files in parallel
Add parallelized implementation for sortoutmappings to improve the time efficiency a little bit
Do not track the number of cache slots if summary option is not given
Change the grain for cahce update loop
Fix a serious issue of generating best paired mapping results, especially when the pair read length differs a lot
Update citation information

For bulk data, the columns are - chrom chrom_start chrom_end N mapq strand + chrom chrom_start chrom_end N mapq strand duplicate_count For single-cell data, the columns are chrom chrom_start chrom_end barcode duplicate_count @@ -119,6 +128,52 @@ chromap --preset hic -x index -r ref.fa -1 read1.fa -2 read2.fa -o aln.pairs ``` Chromap will perform split alignment (**--split-alignment**) on Hi-C reads and output mappings in [pairs][pairs] format (**--pairs**), which is used in [4DN Hi-C data processing pipeline][4DN]. Some Hi-C data analysis pipelines may require the reads are sorted in specific chromosome order other than the one in the index. Therefore, Chromap provides the option **--chr-order** to specify the alignment order, and **--pairs-natural-chr-order** for flipping the pair in the pairs format. +### Summarizing mapping statistics/quality control + +Chromap allows you to summarize the dataset's mapping statistics as well as quality metrics at either a *bulk* or *single cell* level. To enable this feature, users can specify a file path using this option, **--summary [FILE]**, where a csv file will be saved. + +This summary file will output a series of metrics for each barcode (or the overall dataset if it is bulk). Here are the different columns contained within the summary file: + +```sh +barcode,total,duplicate,unmapped,lowmapq,cachehit,fric,estfrip,numcacheslots +``` + +- `barcode` - Barcode label for cell +- `total` - Total number of fragments +- `duplicate` - Number of duplicate fragments +- `unmapped` - Number of unmapped fragments +- `lowmapq` - Number of fragments with a low MAPQ +- `cachehit` - Number of fragments that were found in the chromap cache during alignment +- `fric` - Fraction of fragments in the chromap cache +- `estfrip` - Estimated FRiP value based on a linear model ([See below for more details](#estfrip)) +- `numcacheslots` - Number of unique associated cache slots for this barcode (Relevant feature for doublet detection, [see below for more](#doublet)) + +The summary contains metrics relevant to the mappability of fragments from each barcode. +However, it also contains metrics (`estfrip` and `numcacheslots`) relevant to quality control for chromatin profiling assays like scATAC-seq. These cache-related metrics require overall deep sequencing depth, so it is more useful for single-cell data. +The next two sections briefly describe these two metrics and how they can be useful for users. + +#### Estimating FRiP + +The `estfrip` column in Chromap's summary file represents an estimate of the FRiP score (Fraction of Reads in Peak Regions) computed by Chromap. +Chromap uses a simple multi-variate linear model to estimate the FRiP for each barcode and the features used in this model are `fric`, `duplicate`, `unmapped` and `lowmapq`. + +Typically, the FRiP score is used to assess the quality of chromatin profiles, where typically the higher the FRiP score the better. + +For users, this `estfrip` can be used to quickly gauge the quality of the data by plotting all the values in a histogram and looking to see if you a multi-modal distribution. +In addition, when combining Chromap with downstream analysis tools such as [SnapATAC2](https://github.com/kaizhang/SnapATAC2) that perform clustering, the `estfrip` can be used to quickly identify any specific clusters that are lower quality than the rest. + +**An important note to users**, the `estfrip` values for every barcode should not be taken by themselves and used as the true FRiP score. +These estimates are mainly intended to be used for quality control at a dataset level where we compare different `estfrip` values to each other. + +#### Features to assist in doublet detection + +The `numcacheslots` column in Chromap's summary file estimates the number of unique cache slots queried for each barcode during the alignment. This feature can be useful in assisting users for doublet detection/filtering. + +Typically for doublet detection in single-cell datasets, a simple and naive metric used to identify potential doublets is the number of fragments in cells (i.e. more reads, more likely a doublet). + +Chromap uses the simple intuition that barcodes with higher number of peaks than usual, could be doublets. The number of unique cache slots that are queried can be seen as a proxy for the number of peaks. In our experiments, using `numcacheslots` yields a larger AUC compared using `total` for binary classification of doublets. Therefore, users can potentially use this metric as an additional check/feature along with other doublet-detection specific methods. + + ### Getting help Detailed description of Chromap command line options and optional tags can be displayed by running Chromap with **-h** or be found at the [manpage][manpage].
